checks.s: The agreement identifies the Assignor as Quillex Innovations, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company.
The agreement identifies the Assignee as Verdane Systems, Inc., a Virginia corporation.
The agreement identifies the Escrow Agent as Atlantic Fiduciary Services, Inc., a New York corporation.
The Quillex Innovations, LLC signature block lists Dr. Priya Anand as Managing Member.
The Verdane Systems, Inc. signature block lists Marcus Hale as General Counsel.
The agreement states the total Purchase Price as $14,750,000.00 or $14,750,000.
The agreement states Cash at Closing as $12,362,500.00 or $12,362,500.
The agreement states the Holdback Amount as $2,387,500.00 or $2,387,500.
The agreement states Cash at Closing of $12,362,500, a Holdback Amount of $2,387,500, and a total Purchase Price of $14,750,000, and the two components add up to the total.
The agreement states that the Holdback Amount is deposited with Atlantic Fiduciary Services, Inc. as escrow agent.
The agreement states that the holdback is released 12 months after Closing or on July 15, 2026, assuming a July 15, 2025 Closing.
The agreement provides that holdback release is net of amounts subject to pending or unresolved indemnification claims.
The agreement requires joint written instructions from both parties to the Escrow Agent for holdback release.
The agreement states the Escrow Agent fee is $17,500.
The agreement states that the $17,500 Escrow Agent fee is split equally, with each party paying $8,750, or that each party bears 50% of the fee.
Schedule A lists all 8 granted US utility patents numbered US 11,234,001 through US 11,234,008.
Schedule A lists pending US patent applications with Serial Nos. 17/891,201, 17/891,202, and 17/891,203.
Schedule A lists PCT applications PCT/US2023/044710 and PCT/US2023/044711.
Schedule A indicates that maintenance fees are current for the granted US patents.
Schedule A flags a pending non-final rejection (obviousness) for application Serial No. 17/891,202.
Schedule A states September 30, 2025 as the national-phase entry deadline for the PCT applications.
Schedule B lists QUILLEX SENSORFUSE, Registration No. 6,891,112, Class 9, and TTAB Opposition No. 91,278,455.
Schedule B lists QUILLEX, Registration No. 6,712,330, Class 9.
Schedule B lists FUSIONCORE, Registration No. 6,802,417, Classes 9 and 42.
Schedule B lists the Q-SENSE design mark, Registration No. 6,950,221, Class 9.
Schedule E lists quillex.com, fusioncore.io, and qsense.tech.
Schedule E identifies DomainVault Registrar, LLC as the registrar for all three domain names.
Schedule C lists all 12 copyright registrations numbered TX 9-301-001 through TX 9-301-012.
Schedule C identifies the subject matter as firmware source code versions 1.0 through 6.2.
Schedule D describes the trade secrets as proprietary sensor-fusion calibration algorithms and associated training data sets.
Schedule D references approximately 14 TB of data.
Schedule D references the internal knowledge base designation 'Project Helix.'

Schedule F discloses TTAB Opposition No. 91,278,455, filed by Metrion Analytics Corp. on November 3, 2024, against QUILLEX SENSORFUSE (Reg. No. 6,891,112), and states that it is currently in the discovery phase.
Schedule F discloses the pending non-final office action on patent application Serial No. 17/891,202 and gives February 14, 2026 as the response deadline.
The Assignor's no-pending-or-threatened-litigation representation specifically carves out TTAB Opposition No. 91,278,455 and cross-references Schedule F.
The agreement requires Quillex, after Closing, to assist Verdane in defending the QUILLEX SENSORFUSE mark in TTAB Opposition No. 91,278,455.
The agreement requires Quillex, after Closing, to assist in prosecuting the pending patent applications, including responding to the office action on Serial No. 17/891,202 by February 14, 2026.
The agreement requires Quillex, after Closing, to assist in entering national phase for the PCT applications by September 30, 2025.
The agreement requires Assignor, before Closing, to maintain and prosecute all pending patent applications and PCT applications consistent with past practice.
The pre-closing covenant prohibits Assignor from abandoning any pending application without Assignee's prior written consent.
The indemnification cap for fraud is stated as $14,750,000 or 100% of the Purchase Price.
The indemnification cap for all non-fraud breaches is stated as $7,375,000 or 50% of the Purchase Price.
The indemnification basket is stated as $147,500 or 1% of the Purchase Price.
The indemnification basket is a tipping basket, so once losses exceed the threshold, the indemnifying party is liable from dollar one for the full amount of losses.
The survival period for general representations and warranties is 24 months post-Closing.
The survival period for IP ownership and authority representations is 48 months post-Closing.
Fraud claims survive indefinitely, without a time limitation.
The non-competition covenant lasts 3 years post-Closing.
The non-competition covenant is limited to sensor-fusion technology in the autonomous-vehicle vertical, or substantially equivalent scope.
The non-competition covenant is limited geographically to the United States and the European Union.
The agreement states that it is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.
The dispute resolution clause provides for binding arbitration under AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules.
The agreement states that the arbitration is seated in Wilmington, Delaware.
The agreement specifies a three-arbitrator panel for claims exceeding $1,000,000 and a sole arbitrator for claims at or below $1,000,000.
The agreement states July 15, 2025 as the Closing Date.
The assignment clause makes an outright, irrevocable transfer of all right, title, and interest in the Assigned IP, rather than a license or conditional transfer.
The assignment clause covers patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, domain names, and associated goodwill.
The Assignor represents that all employees and contractors who contributed to the Assigned IP executed valid IP assignment agreements in favor of Quillex, or substantially equivalent agreements.
The Assignor represents that no open-source code is incorporated into the firmware source code in a manner that imposes copyleft or similar obligations on the Assigned IP.
The Closing and Deliverables section lists a short-form patent assignment for USPTO recording and references Exhibit A.
The Closing and Deliverables section lists a short-form trademark assignment for USPTO recording and references Exhibit B.
The Closing and Deliverables section lists a short-form copyright assignment for USCO recording and references Exhibit C.
The Closing and Deliverables section lists domain transfer authorization letter(s) to DomainVault Registrar, LLC and references Exhibit D.

The agreement includes a trade-secret delivery protocol or covenant addressing transfer to Verdane, at or promptly following Closing, of approximately 14 TB of Project Helix calibration algorithms and training data sets.
The Assignor represents that it owns and has valid title to all Assigned IP, free and clear of encumbrances except Permitted Encumbrances.
The Assignor represents that the Assigned IP does not infringe third-party IP rights.
The Assignor represents the validity and enforceability of the IP rights in the Assigned IP.
The Assignor represents that maintenance fees are current for all granted patents.
The Assignor represents that the Assigned IP is sufficient for the business as conducted.

The agreement takes a Verdane-favorable Assignee/buyer posture, with broad Assignor representations and covenants, robust indemnification rights for Assignee, and protective provisions favoring the buyer.
The agreement represents that Assignee has authority to enter into it and that its execution does not conflict with Assignee's organizational documents or applicable law.
The agreement includes an entire agreement clause.
The agreement includes an amendment/waiver clause requiring written form.
The agreement includes a severability clause.
The agreement includes an assignment restrictions clause.
The agreement includes a counterparts clause.
The agreement includes a further assurances clause.
The agreement includes a notices provision with addresses for both parties.
The notice address for Quillex Innovations, LLC is 400 Innovation Drive, Suite 310, Wilmington, DE 19801.
The notice address for Verdane Systems, Inc. is 8700 Westpark Boulevard, Suite 600, McLean, VA 22102.
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Assigned IP' tailored to the Quillex/Verdane transaction.
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Patents.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Trademarks.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Copyrights.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Trade Secrets.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Domain Names.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Know-How.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Purchase Price.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Holdback Amount.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Escrow Agent.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Closing Date.'
The Definitions section includes a defined term for 'Permitted Encumbrances.'
No bracketed placeholders from the template remain in the deliverable.
No template drafting notes or comments remain in the deliverable.
The trademark assignment expressly transfers goodwill together with the trademarks.
The escrow provisions cross-reference a separate Escrow Agreement executed concurrently with the IP Assignment Agreement, rather than setting out full escrow mechanics in-line.
The indemnification section states that indemnification is the exclusive remedy for breaches of representations and warranties.
The exclusive-remedy provision carves out fraud and equitable relief.
The recitals describe Verdane's acquisition of Quillex's entire IP portfolio as an asset-purchase transaction by outright assignment.
The recitals identify the IP as including patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, and domain names.
The recitals reference the Purchase Price consideration as cash at closing and a holdback.
